title: A heart test for bounded-below left t-exact transformations
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\Phi,\Psi:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ be triangulated functors [def-weil-triangulated-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], with specified natural shift isomorphisms $\xi_E:\Phi(E[1])\cong\Phi(E)[1]$ and $\zeta_E:\Psi(E[1])\cong\Psi(E)[1]$. Let $\eta:\Phi\to\Psi$ be a natural transformation satisfying $\zeta_E\circ\eta_{E[1]}=\eta_E[1]\circ\xi_E$ for every $E$. Assume both functors preserve every lower cohomology bound: if $H^q(M)=0$ for $q<n$, then $H^q(\Phi M)=H^q(\Psi M)=0$ for $q<n$, for every integer $n$ and every $M\in D^+(\mathcal A)$.

Let $E\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ and suppose $\eta_{H^q(E)[0]}$ is invertible for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, where $H^q(E)[0]$ means the cohomology object placed in degree zero. Then $\eta_E$ is invertible. More precisely, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$, the upper truncation inclusion $c_m:\tau_{\le m}E\to E$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] makes both $H^m(\Phi c_m)$ and $H^m(\Psi c_m)$ invertible, $\eta_{\tau_{\le m}E}$ is invertible, and naturality gives
$$H^m(\eta_E)=H^m(\Psi c_m)\circ H^m(\eta_{\tau_{\le m}E})\circ H^m(\Phi c_m)^{-1}.$$
The statement allows negative lower bounds and does not assume an upper bound on $E$ or preservation of any infinite limit by either functor.
